title: Ezekiel Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
Ezekiel prophesies against the land of Israel
The sword of the LORD is drawn forth
Ezekiel is to sigh with bitterness
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned is found in Ezekiel 21:1 where it states, 'And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying.'

questions.question: What is Ezekiel instructed to set his face toward?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to set his face toward Jerusalem as stated in Ezekiel 21:2.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do to the land of Israel?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 21:3, the LORD says, 'Behold, I am against thee, and will draw forth my sword out of his sheath.'

questions.question: From whom will the LORD cut off?
options: Both the righteous and the wicked
Neither the righteous nor the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Both the righteous and the wicked
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:3 states that the LORD will cut off 'from thee the righteous and the wicked.'

questions.question: Where shall the sword of the LORD go forth from?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:4 mentions that the sword will go forth 'out of his sheath.'

questions.question: What will all flesh know?
options: That the sword of the LORD has been drawn
questions.correctAnswer: That the sword of the LORD has been drawn
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:5 states, 'That all flesh may know that I the LORD have drawn forth my sword out of his sheath.'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel have to do with bitterness?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 21:6, it says, 'Sigh therefore, thou son of man, with the breaking of thy loins; and with bitterness sigh before their eyes.'

questions.question: What will happen when they ask Ezekiel why he sighs?
options: He will say it is for joy
He will tell them about the tidings
questions.correctAnswer: He will tell them about the tidings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:7 mentions that he shall answer, 'For the tidings; because it cometh.'

questions.question: What is the sword described as in Ezekiel 21:9?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:9 states, 'Say, A sword, a sword is sharpened, and also furbished.'

questions.question: What does the sword's sharpening lead to?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:10 indicates that it is 'sharpened to make a sore slaughter.'

questions.question: What is the sword given to be handled for?
options: To give it into the hand of the slayer
questions.correctAnswer: To give it into the hand of the slayer
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:11 states, 'this sword is sharpened, and it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the slayer.'

questions.question: The sword of the LORD will return to its sheath.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:5 says, 'it shall not return any more,' indicating it will not return to the sheath.

questions.question: Ezekiel is referred to as 'son of man' in this chapter.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is addressed as 'son of man' in Ezekiel 21:2 and 21:6.

questions.question: The sword is described as being both dull and rusty.
questions.explanation: The sword is described as 'sharpened' and 'furbished,' not dull or rusty, as seen in Ezekiel 21:9.

questions.question: Ezekiel is commanded to drop his word toward the wicked.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is commanded to drop his word toward the holy places, not specifically toward the wicked, as mentioned in Ezekiel 21:2.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is commanded to the son of man in Ezekiel 21:12?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it directly states in Ezekiel 21:12, 'Cry and howl, son of man: for it shall be upon my people...'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 21:13 promise will happen if one contemplates the sword's contempt for the rod?
options: It will be a sign of strength
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:13 states, 'it shall be no more, saith the Lord GOD', indicating the finality of the sword's action.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 21:15 say is set against all their gates?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:15 mentions, 'I have set the point of the sword against all their gates...'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 21:16, what choices are presented?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:16 directly states, 'Go thee one way or other...'

questions.question: What is the significance of smiting hands together as mentioned in Ezekiel 21:14?
options: To signify the seriousness of the prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: To signify the seriousness of the prophecy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:14 instructs to smite hands together, emphasizing the gravity of the situation being prophesied.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 21:18 state about the word of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:18 starts with, 'The word of the LORD came unto me again...'

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 21:19 instruct the son of man to do?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 21:19, the instruction is to 'appoint thee two ways,' indicating a choice in the prophecy.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 21:21 say the king of Babylon did at the parting of the way?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:21 states, 'the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination...'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 21:22, what was at the king's right hand?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:22 specifies, 'At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem...'

questions.question: What emotion does Ezekiel 21:7 describe that the people will feel when they hear the tidings?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:7 states that 'every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble,' indicating fear.

questions.question: In preparing for judgment, what does Ezekiel 21:6 command the son of man to do?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:6 instructs to 'sigh therefore, thou son of man, with the breaking of thy loins; and with bitterness sigh before their eyes.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of the sword as mentioned in Ezekiel 21:10?
options: To cut off the righteous only
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:10 states, 'It is sharpened to make a sore slaughter; it is furbished that it may glitter...'

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel 21:5 states that the sword will return to its sheath?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:5 declares, 'it shall not return any more,' indicating the finality of the judgment.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel 21:4 mentions only the wicked will be cut off?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:4 states that both the righteous and the wicked will be cut off, not just the wicked.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel 21:11 talks about the sword being given into the hand of the slayer?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:11 mentions that the sword is sharpened and furbished 'to give it into the hand of the slayer,' hence this statement is correct.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 21:23, what will the false divination be like to those who have sworn oaths?
options: As a false divination in their sight
questions.correctAnswer: As a false divination in their sight
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:23 states it shall be unto them as a false divination in their sight, specifically to those who have sworn oaths.

questions.question: Why does the Lord say the iniquity of the people will be called to remembrance in Ezekiel 21:24?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:24 states that because their iniquity is remembered and their transgressions discovered, their sins appear in all their doings.

questions.question: Who is described as the 'profane wicked prince of Israel' whose day has come in Ezekiel 21:25?
options: The profane wicked prince of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The profane wicked prince of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:25 explicitly calls this person the 'profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come'.

questions.question: What does God command to be removed from the prince in Ezekiel 21:26?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:26 commands to remove the diadem and take off the crown from the prince.

questions.question: How many times will God overturn the kingdom according to Ezekiel 21:27?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:27 uses repetition 'I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it' indicating thrice.

questions.question: What is the fate of the Ammonites as prophesied in Ezekiel 21:31?
options: They will be delivered into the hand of brutish men
They will be allies of Israel
They will be blessed by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into the hand of brutish men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:31 states God will pour out indignation and deliver the Ammonites into the hand of brutish men skilled to destroy.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'diadem' (Ezekiel 21:26) mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'diadem' refers to a royal crown or headband symbolizing kingship as used in Ezekiel 21:26.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Ezekiel 21:27 with the repetition of 'overturn'?
questions.explanation: The repetition of the word 'overturn' at the start of successive phrases exemplifies anaphora in Ezekiel 21:27.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine judgment by the sword as in Ezekiel 21:3?
questions.explanation: Revelation 19:15 speaks of a sharp sword from the mouth of Christ to strike the nations, echoing Ezekiel 21:3's theme of divine judgment by sword.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage fulfills the prophecy of the removal of the diadem and the overturning of the kingdom in Ezekiel 21:26-27?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:27-30 records the release of Jehoiachin from prison, symbolizing the removal and restoration of kingship, fulfilling Ezekiel 21:26-27.

questions.question: What instruction precedes the prophecy about the Ammonites in Ezekiel 21:28?
options: Remove the diadem and take off the crown
Prophesy and smite thine hands together
Appoint thee two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon
Set thy face toward Jerusalem and drop thy word
questions.correctAnswer: Appoint thee two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:19-21 instructs to appoint two ways for the sword of Babylon before the prophecy against the Ammonites in verse 28.

questions.question: What is the significance of the sword being 'furbished' in Ezekiel 21:10 and 21:28?
options: It symbolizes preparation for slaughter and judgment
It indicates the sword is old and rusty
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes preparation for slaughter and judgment
questions.explanation: The term 'furbished' means sharpened and polished, indicating readiness for slaughter and judgment as in Ezekiel 21:10 and 21:28.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 21:23-24 function as a literary inclusio in the chapter?
options: By framing the sword imagery with divine judgment
By repeating the mention of false divination and remembrance of iniquity
By starting and ending with the city of Jerusalem
By quoting the same phrase twice
questions.correctAnswer: By repeating the mention of false divination and remembrance of iniquity
questions.explanation: Verses 21:23 and 21:24 both mention false divination and remembrance of iniquity, creating an inclusio framing the message about judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 21:32 declares that the Ammonites' blood shall be in the midst of the land and they shall be no more remembered.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:32 states the Ammonites' blood shall be in the midst of the land and they shall be no more remembered.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 21:5 says the sword of the Lord will return to its sheath after the destruction.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:5 states the sword shall not return any more, indicating it will not return to its sheath.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 21:3 teach about God’s nature in relation to justice and judgment?
options: God’s judgment is impartial, cutting off both the righteous and the wicked
God only punishes the wicked while sparing the righteous
God’s justice is delayed until the final day of judgment
God’s wrath is arbitrary and without cause
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is impartial, cutting off both the righteous and the wicked
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:3 states that God will cut off both the righteous and the wicked, showing His impartial and sovereign judgment over all people.

questions.question: What doctrine about the certainty of divine judgment is taught in Ezekiel 21:5?
options: God’s judgment is final and will not return to its sheath
God’s judgment can be reversed through repentance
God’s wrath is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is final and will not return to its sheath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:5 emphasizes that God’s sword of judgment has been drawn and shall not return, indicating the irrevocability of His divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the relationship between divine wrath and human response is illustrated in Ezekiel 21:7?
options: Divine judgment causes fear and helplessness in the human heart
God’s wrath can be ignored without consequence
Human effort can overcome divine judgment
Divine wrath results in immediate destruction without warning
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment causes fear and helplessness in the human heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:7 describes how every heart will melt, hands become feeble, and knees weak, showing the deep human effect of encountering God’s judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 21:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 21:17, God declares that He controls His fury and has decreed all that will happen, demonstrating His supreme sovereignty.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ezekiel 21:26 where the removal of the diadem and crown is decreed?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:26 shows God’s justice in removing the crown due to iniquity, reflecting His righteous judgment against unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 21:19–22 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine sovereignty over empires in redemptive history?
options: It affirms God’s control over the rise and fall of worldly kingdoms
It denies any divine involvement in political affairs
It suggests empires operate independently of God’s will
It implies Babylon’s victory is purely by military might
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God’s control over the rise and fall of worldly kingdoms
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:19–22 depicts God’s orchestration of the king of Babylon’s decisions, illustrating divine sovereignty over empires throughout redemptive history.

questions.question: How does the imagery of the sword in Ezekiel 21:9–11 prepare for the fulfillment of judgment against Israel as seen in the Babylonian exile?
options: The sword symbolizes the impending and inevitable judgment by Babylon
The sword represents Israel’s military victory
The sword is a metaphor for peace and restoration
The sword is a symbol of Israel’s spiritual triumph
questions.correctAnswer: The sword symbolizes the impending and inevitable judgment by Babylon
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 21:9–11, the sharpened and furbished sword denotes the coming slaughter, directly preparing for the Babylonian conquest and exile.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 21:25 and 21:26 teach about divine justice and kingship?
options: God’s justice results in the removal and replacement of unfaithful rulers
Kingship is permanent and unaffected by sin
God’s justice spares rulers regardless of their sin
The king’s power is autonomous and independent of God
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice results in the removal and replacement of unfaithful rulers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:25–26 show that due to iniquity, God commands the removal of the diadem and crown, signaling the end of a corrupt ruler’s reign and foreshadowing divine appointment of the rightful king.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 21:28 and 21:31 teach about God’s judgment on the Ammonites?
options: God’s judgment is righteous, vindicating His holiness by punishing nations for their sins
God’s judgment is arbitrary and without reason
God shows mercy by sparing the Ammonites
God’s judgment is symbolic and will not be fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is righteous, vindicating His holiness by punishing nations for their sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:28 and 21:31 declare the sword is drawn against the Ammonites because of their sins, demonstrating righteous judgment consistent with God’s holy character.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine judgment and human rebellion is taught in Ezekiel 21:23 and 21:24?
options: Human iniquity leads to inevitable divine judgment despite false hopes
God forgets human sins and withholds judgment
False prophecy can overturn God’s decrees
questions.correctAnswer: Human iniquity leads to inevitable divine judgment despite false hopes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:23–24 explains that although Babylon’s divination appears false to some, God remembers Israel’s sins and brings judgment, affirming that human iniquity provokes divine justice.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Ezekiel 21:4–5 teaches that God’s judgment is indiscriminate and unjust. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is sovereign and all-encompassing, but serves a righteous purpose
God’s judgment is unfair and shows favoritism
God’s sword will return to the sheath if mercy is shown
God’s judgment is based on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is sovereign and all-encompassing, but serves a righteous purpose
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:4–5 states that God’s sword cuts off both righteous and wicked to show His sovereignty and the seriousness of judgment, not injustice or favoritism.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic symbolism is taught in Ezekiel 21:14 regarding the ‘sword of the slain’?
options: Prophetic actions symbolize the certainty and severity of coming judgment
Prophetic symbolism is optional and non-essential
Symbolism in prophecy always predicts immediate events
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic actions symbolize the certainty and severity of coming judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:14 commands the prophet to smite his hands and double the sword, symbolizing the intensive judgment coming upon the slain and leaders, underscoring prophetic symbolic actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed in Ezekiel 21:32 where God says the Ammonites shall be no more remembered?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:32 shows God’s judicial wrath as He declares the Ammonites will be destroyed and forgotten due to their rebellion against Him.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine foreknowledge and human agency is taught in Ezekiel 21:21 where the king of Babylon uses divination before battle?
options: God’s sovereignty encompasses even pagan practices, guiding history to fulfill His purposes
Human decisions are completely independent of divine will
Divination is a reliable source of truth
God is unaware of the king’s actions and plans
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty encompasses even pagan practices, guiding history to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:21 describes Babylon’s king using divination, yet the broader context shows God controls the outcome, revealing His sovereign orchestration over human affairs.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 21:12 contribute to the theme of covenantal accountability in Israel’s history?
options: It calls for lament because God’s sword will bring terror to His covenant people due to their sins
It promises immediate restoration without consequences
It denies any punishment for covenant violations
It excuses Israel’s sin because of God’s mercy
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for lament because God’s sword will bring terror to His covenant people due to their sins
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 21:12 commands the prophet to cry and howl because the sword is against God’s people, reflecting covenantal accountability and judgment for their transgressions.
